title: "Does humidity make heat drive electricity demand harder? Evidence from ERCOT, 2025"
format: html
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(riem)
```

## Research question

Does the effect of temperature on ERCOT electricity demand depend on how humid the air is?
I modeled 5 PM demand on warm days (≥ 65°F) as a function of temperature (continuous),
dew point (categorical: dry / sticky / muggy), and their interaction.

## Causal assumptions (DAG)

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    Season --> Temp[Temperature]
    Season --> Dew[Dew point]
    Hour[Time of day] --> Temp
    Hour --> Dew
    Hour --> Demand
    Temp --> Demand
    Dew --> Demand

```

I assumed that season affects demand only through weather, so including temperature and dew point
blocks the backdoor paths through season. Time of day is held constant by using only 5 PM data.

## 1. Data

### Electricity demand (EIA-930)

```{r}
#| label: read-eia

# load demand data and filter to ERCOT
ercot <- read_csv(c("data/EIA930_BALANCE_2025_Jan_Jun.csv",
                    "data/EIA930_BALANCE_2025_Jul_Dec.csv")) |>
  filter(`Balancing Authority` == "ERCO") |>
  # create datetime column
  mutate(datetime = mdy_hms(`UTC Time at End of Hour`))
```

### Weather (ASOS airport stations via riem)

```{r}
#| label: read-weather

# put texas stations into a list
stations <- c("IAH", "DFW", "SAT", "AUS")

weather <- stations |>
  map(function(station) riem_measures(station,
                                date_start = "2025-01-01",
                                date_end   = "2026-01-01")) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  # round observation times up to match EIA's hour-ending timestamps
  mutate(datetime = ceiling_date(valid, "hour")) |>
  # average within each station and hour
  summarise(across(c(tmpf, dwpf), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .by = c(station, datetime)) |>
  # then average across the four stations
  summarise(across(c(tmpf, dwpf), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .by = datetime)
```

### Join and check

```{r}
#| label: join

# join data
all_data <- left_join(ercot, weather, by = join_by(datetime))

# check nas 
sum(is.na(all_data$datetime))
sum(is.na(all_data$`Demand (MW)`))
sum(is.na(all_data$tmpf))
sum(is.na(all_data$dwpf))
```

## 2. Analysis sample

Keep hour ending 5 PM Central which is near the daily peak (to control for how time of day impacts demand and temperature), and keep temperature at or above 65°F so the temperature–demand relationship is based solely off of cooling.

```{r}
#| label: model-data
model_data <- all_data |>
  mutate(local_hour = hour(with_tz(datetime, "America/Chicago"))) |>
  filter(local_hour == 17,
         tmpf >= 65,
         !is.na(dwpf), !is.na(`Demand (MW)`)) |>
  mutate(dew_bin = cut(dwpf,
                       breaks = c(-Inf, 55, 65, Inf),
                       labels = c("Dry", "Sticky", "Muggy")),
         tmpf_c  = tmpf - mean(tmpf))

# Group sizes and temperature range within each dew point bin
model_data |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            min_temp = min(tmpf),
            max_temp = max(tmpf),
            .by = dew_bin) |>
  arrange(dew_bin)
```

## 3. Exploratory analysis

### Summary statistics

```{r}
#| label: summary-stats
model_data |>
  select(`Demand (MW)`,
         `Temperature (°F)` = tmpf,
         `Dew point (°F)`   = dwpf) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable") |>
  summarise(n      = sum(!is.na(value)),
            mean   = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd     = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            min    = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            max    = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            .by = variable)
```

### Distributions

```{r}
#| label: histograms
ggplot(model_data, aes(x = `Demand (MW)`)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(title = "5 PM demand, warm days", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

ggplot(model_data, aes(x = tmpf)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "firebrick", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "5 PM temperature, warm days", x = "Temperature (°F)", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

## 4. Model

```{r}
#| label: model
model <- lm(`Demand (MW)` ~ tmpf_c * dew_bin, data = model_data)

summary(model)
```

### Does the interaction improve the model?

```{r}
#| label: interaction-test
model_no_int <- lm(`Demand (MW)` ~ tmpf_c + dew_bin, data = model_data)
anova(model_no_int, model)
```


## 5. Fitted model

```{r}
#| label: fitted-plot
pred_grid <- model_data |>
  reframe(tmpf = seq(min(tmpf), max(tmpf), length.out = 100), .by = dew_bin) |>
  mutate(tmpf_c = tmpf - mean(model_data$tmpf))

preds <- pred_grid |>
  bind_cols(as_tibble(predict(model, newdata = pred_grid, interval = "confidence")))

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = model_data,
             aes(x = tmpf, y = `Demand (MW)`, color = dew_bin),
             alpha = 0.5, size = 1.8) +
  geom_ribbon(data = preds,
              aes(x = tmpf, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr, fill = dew_bin),
              alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = preds,
            aes(x = tmpf, y = fit, color = dew_bin),
            linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "plasma", end = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", end = 0.85) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(title = "ERCOT 5 PM demand vs. temperature by dew point, 2025",
       subtitle = "Days ≥ 65°F; lines are fitted values, bands are 95% CIs (not autocorrelation-corrected)",
       x = "Temperature (°F)",
       y = "Demand (MW)",
       color = "Dew point", fill = "Dew point") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, size = 3)))
```
